question: Reye's syndrome is associated with {{c1::hepatic encephalopathy}}. ASPIRIN
answer:
WHY ASPIRIN CONTRAINDICATED IN VIRAL INFECTION IN CHILDREN?



An acute non-inflammatory encephalopathy and hepatopathy, with no reasonable

Reye's syndrome usually occurs in children who have had a recent viral infection, such as chickenpox or the flu. Taking aspirin to treat such an infection greatly increases the risk of Reye's

The exact reason behind the syndrome is yet to be known, Inherited metabolic errors and acetylsalicylic acid (also known as aspirin) are thought to be the reason. Acetylsalicylic acid molecules are metabolised in the liver cells. It is then altered to salicylate which yields several metabolytes.

symptom of Reye's

⚫ DIARRHEA AND RAPID breathing • Continous vomiting ⚫ sleepiness / lethargy Irritability/ Aggressiveness Confusion, Disorientation Paralysis in arm/legs • Decreased LOC (coma) EDEMA INCREASED ICP. • Hallucination • Seizures
